cards.explanation: The answer is the priests. The LORD says, “Ask the priests for a ruling.” Haggai, the prophet getting this word, doesn't offer his own opinion, friends. He takes the question straight to the people the LORD named (Haggai 2:11).

The answer is False. The question is whether the food becomes holy, and “No,” replied the priests. The consecrated meat can touch bread, stew, wine, oil or any other food, and none of it becomes holy. One word, friends, and it settles it (Haggai 2:12).

The answer is defiled. Haggai asks about someone defiled by contact with a corpse, and the priests answer, “Yes, it becomes defiled…” Notice the shift from the first question, friends. A flat no turns into a clear yes. This one is a heavy subject, so I'll just say plainly that the ruling is clear (Haggai 2:13).

The answer is True. Haggai says, “…and so it is with every work of their hands; whatever they offer there is defiled.” The priests' rulings were about food, and now Haggai applies them to the people and the nation. This is a hard word, friends, and the LORD declares it plainly (Haggai 2:14).

The answer is before one stone sat on another. The LORD says, “Now consider carefully from this day forward: Before one stone was placed on another in the temple of the LORD…” He points them back to that moment before the first stone sat on another. Then He tells them what they saw from that time on (Haggai 2:15).

The answer is False. Someone came expecting a heap of twenty ephahs of grain and there were but ten. The winepress told the same story, friends: someone came to draw out fifty baths and there were but twenty. Half a heap or less, and nobody likes that math (Haggai 2:16).

The answer is that they did not turn to Him. The LORD says, “…but you did not turn to Me, declares the LORD.” He had struck all the work of their hands with blight, mildew and hail. And through all of that, friends, the text says they did not turn to Him (Haggai 2:17).

The answer is that the foundation of the LORD's temple was laid. The LORD names the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month as “…the day the foundation of the LORD’s temple was laid…” That's the very day He is speaking to them, friends. The foundation is down, and He tells them to consider carefully from this day on (Haggai 2:18).

The answer is False. “The vine, the fig, the pomegranate, and the olive tree have not yet yielded fruit.” They haven't yielded yet, friends. And then the LORD turns it around with a promise (Haggai 2:19).

The answer is bless, and what a way to end, friends. The LORD says, “But from this day on, I will bless you.” The barn question and the plants that have not yet yielded fruit come first, and then comes that promise. I think it's a good one to read twice (Haggai 2:19).
